organizations.name: Adaptive Wilderness Within Reach

organizations.name: Advocating Change Together, Inc.
organizations.summary: Advocating Change Together is a disability rights nonprofit in Saint Paul, started in 1979 by people with and without disabilities. It supports leadership by people with disabilities. It runs Self-Advocates Minnesota, a statewide network of self-advocacy groups.
organizations.whoItServes: Its mission is to support the leadership of people with disabilities to fight ableism and build inclusive communities.
organizations.whereItWorks: Statewide, from an office in Saint Paul. Its 2020 Innovation Grant served the Twin Cities metro area and St. Cloud.
services: Self-Advocates Minnesota network of self-advocacy groups

Remembering With Dignity program
Side by Side People's Chorus

organizations.whyItMattersForStaff: Staff planning self-advocacy training, housing choice education, or ways to include people with disabilities in policy work may connect with this organization.

organizations.name: The Arc Minnesota
organizations.summary: The Arc Minnesota promotes and protects the human rights of people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. It offers advocacy, housing help, self-advocacy support, mentoring and small grants to individuals. It also runs Arc's Value Village thrift stores.
organizations.whoItServes: It says it supports people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families across the state.
organizations.whereItWorks: Statewide, with regional offices.

Housing services, including Housing Access Services and crisis housing help
Self-advocacy and a peer-to-peer mentor program
Scholarships and small grants to individuals
Statewide public policy advocacy

Helps people with disabilities find and keep housing of their choice. The 2023 report names The Arc Minnesota and United Care Services as the two grantees.

organizations.name: Udac Inc
organizations.summary: Udac Inc is a nonprofit in Duluth that helps people with disabilities find jobs and take part in community life. It was incorporated in 1969 as United Day Activity Center. After the pandemic it closed its special minimum wage program and now focuses on community inclusion and independent employment.
organizations.whoItServes: Udac says it works to create a community where opportunity is accessible to individuals of all abilities.
organizations.whereItWorks: Duluth. Its 2024 Innovation Grant project served Carlton, Lake and St. Louis counties in greater Minnesota.

Career and life coaching
Benefits counseling
Community integration activities

organizations.name: Institute on Community Integration, University of Minnesota
organizations.summary: The Institute on Community Integration is a research and training center at the University of Minnesota. It is a federally designated University Center for Excellence in Developmental Disabilities. It builds and shares knowledge with service providers, policymakers, educators and families.
organizations.whoItServes: In its own words, it works so that "people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and those who face similar barriers to inclusion can thrive."
organizations.whereItWorks: Based in Minneapolis. Its Minnesota Transformation Initiative work is statewide; it also works nationally and internationally.
services: Research and training on community living and employment
Early childhood and education policy work
Technical assistance to service providers, counties and tribal nations
Training, peer mentoring and toolkits for providers, self-advocates and families

withTheDivision.program: Provider Reinvention Grant program: Minnesota Transformation Initiative
withTheDivision.amount: $3 million (as reported by the Institute in May 2022)
withTheDivision.what: The Department of Human Services hired the Institute as the technical assistance firm for the Provider Reinvention Grant program and to carry out the Minnesota Transformation Initiative. The work helps nearly two dozen service providers expand customized, integrated employment and move away from wages below the minimum wage, with partners the University of Massachusetts Boston, The Arc Minnesota, Strengths at Work and Quillo.

organizations.whyItMattersForStaff: Staff working on Employment First, competitive integrated employment, or providers moving away from wages below the minimum wage may connect with this organization. It runs the Minnesota Transformation Initiative technical assistance center.

organizations.name: Upstream Arts Inc
organizations.summary: Upstream Arts Inc was a Minneapolis nonprofit that used the arts to work with people with disabilities in schools, adult programs and the community. Its website now says it has closed after 20 years because the resources to keep the work going were no longer in place.
organizations.whoItServes: Its stated mission was to use the creative arts to activate and amplify the voice and choice of individuals with disabilities. It worked with students, adults with disabilities, and the parents, staff and educators who support them.
organizations.whereItWorks: Minneapolis and Saint Paul area, with the most school work in Minneapolis Public Schools. It also had programs in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.
services: Arts residencies in special education and inclusive classrooms
Arts workshops for adults on self-advocacy, work skills and community life
Sexual violence prevention and healthy relationships program for the disability community
Training for educators and service providers

withTheDivision.what: Called The Art of Prevention. The project aimed to build a culture of sexual violence prevention in adult day programs for adults with intellectual disabilities, through healthy relationship residencies, staff training on consent and bodily autonomy, and talks with program leaders.

organizations.whyItMattersForStaff: Staff reviewing past Innovation Grant work on sexual violence prevention in adult day programs may look at this project. The organization has closed, so it is not a current referral.
